Kursplan (en)












KursplanLäsår25/2626/27
Course syllabus
Cloud Computing
Molnsystem
FRTN90, 7.5 credits, A (Second Cycle)

Valid for: 2026/27
Faculty: Faculty of Engineering LTH
Decided by: PLED F/Pi
Date of Decision: 2026-04-14
    
  
General Information

Depth of study relative to the degree requirements:  Second cycle, in-depth level of the course cannot be classified
      
      
Elective for: C4-sec, C4-pvt, D4-se, D4-pv, D4-ns, MMSR2
Language of instruction: The course will be given in English
    
  
Aim
Understand fundamental concepts within cloud computing and large parallel computer systems, explain their characteristics, and apply them for real-world applications.
Learning outcomes
Knowledge and understanding
      For a passing grade the student must
be able to show basic knowledge about different kinds of cloud systems and their properties,be able to demonstrate basic knowledge about the cloud technology ecosystem, be able to reason about about faults, redundancy, and recovery in cloud applications, be able to show basic knowledge about the technologies underpinning cloud computing.
Competences and skills
      For a passing grade the student must
be able to use terminology and abstractions for modelling cloud system and characterize their behavior,be able to build efficient, secure, and robust cloud applications,be able to design, implement, and deploy a real-world cloud application.
Judgement and approach
      For a passing grade the student must
be able to reason around properties of cloud systems with respect to performance and security,be able to reason around sustainability and resource efficiency,show basic understanding of trade-offs and limitations with the concepts and technologies that are used in design of cloud applications.
Contents
Overview of the cloud market space and fundamental conceptsUsage of basic cloud servicesData center and hardwareResource virtualization (CPU, network, and storage)Automation and orchestrationDesign principles for micro services and cloud native applicationsHands-on experience with standard tools, e.g., KubernetesDevOps-principles

Grading scale: UG - (U, G) - (Fail, Pass)
Assessment: Passed home assignments (3) and passed project.

The examiner, in consultation with Disability Support Services, may deviate from the regular form of examination in order to provide a permanently disabled student with a form of examination equivalent to that of a student without a disability.

Admission

Admission requirements: 

EDAA01 Programming - Second Course or EDAA30 Programming in Java - Second Course

Assumed prior knowledge: 
        EDAF90 Web Programming and EITA25 Computer Security and (EITF45 Computer Communication or ETSF10 Internet Protocols)
        
The number of participants is limited to: 100
Selection: Completed university credits within the programme. Priority is given to students enrolled on programmes that include the course in their curriculum.

Reading list

Dan C. Marinescu: Cloud Computing - Theory and Practice. Boston: Morgan Kaufmann, 2022, ISBN: 9780323852777.
Brendan Burns, Joe Beda, Kelsey Hightower, Lachlan Evenson: Kubernetes - Up and Running (3rd ed.). 2022, ISBN: 9781098110208.
